readings.title: Shamgar
readings.subtitle: The Ox-Goad Deliverer
readings.text: [Judges 3:31] And after him was Shamgar son of Anath, who smote six hundred men of the Philistines with an ox-goad. And he too saved Israel.

readings.title: Deborah and Baraq
readings.subtitle: The Prophecy Against Sisera
readings.text: [Judges 4:1] And the children of Israel again did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, when Ehud was dead. [2] So <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sold them into the hand of Jabin sovereign of Kenaʽan, who reigned in Ḥatsor. And the commander of his army was Sisera, who dwelt in Ḥarosheth Hagoyim. [3] And the children of Israel cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for he had nine hundred chariots of iron, and for twenty years he harshly oppressed the children of Israel. [4] And Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time. [5] And she was dwelling under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Běyth Ěl in the mountains of Ephraim. And the children of Israel came up to her for right-ruling. [6] And she sent and called for Baraq son of Abinoam from Qeḏesh in Naphtali, and said to him, “Has not <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Israel commanded, <dq>‘Go, and you shall draw toward Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men of the sons of Naphtali and of the sons of Zebulun?</dq> [7] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall draw unto you Sisera, the commander of Jabin’s army, with his chariots and his multitude at the River Qishon, and <dn>I</dn> shall give him into your hand’?</dq>” [8] And Baraq said to her, “If you go with me, then I shall go; but if you do not go with me, I do not go.” [9] And she said, “I shall certainly go with you. Only, there shall be no glory for you in the journey you are taking, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is going to sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.” And Deborah arose and went with Baraq to Qeḏesh. [10] And Baraq called Zebulun and Naphtali to Qeḏesh. And he went up with ten thousand men under his command, and Deborah went up with him. [11] Now Ḥeber the Qěynite, of the children of Ḥobab the father-in-law of Mosheh, had separated himself from the Qěynites and pitched his tent near the terebinth tree at Tsaʽanannim, which is beside Qeḏesh. [12] And they reported to Sisera that Baraq son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor. [13] And Sisera called all his chariots, nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people who were with him, from Ḥarosheth Hagoyim to the River Qishon. [14] And Deborah said to Baraq, “Rise! For this is the day in which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given Sisera into your hand. Has not <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gone out before you?” So Baraq went down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men following him. [15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> confused Sisera and all his chariots and all his army with the edge of the sword before Baraq. And Sisera alighted from his chariot and fled away on foot. [16] And Baraq pursued the chariots and the army as far as Ḥarosheth Hagoyim, and all the army of Sisera fell by the edge of the sword, not one was left. [17] But Sisera had fled on foot to the tent of Yaʽěl, the wife of Ḥeber the Qěynite, for there was peace between Jabin sovereign of Ḥatsor and the house of Ḥeber the Qěynite. [18] And Yaʽěl went out to meet Sisera, and said to him, “Turn aside, my master, turn aside to me, do not fear.” And when he had turned aside with her into the tent, she covered him with a blanket. [19] And he said to her, “Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty.” And she opened a bottle of milk, and gave him a drink, and covered him. [20] And he said to her, “Stand at the door of the tent, and it shall be that if any man comes and asks you, and says, ‘Is there a man here?’ you shall say, ‘No.’ ” [21] But Yaʽěl, Ḥeber’s wife, took a tent peg and took a hammer in her hand, and went softly to him and drove the peg into his temple, and it went down into the ground – for he was fast asleep and weary – and he died. [22] And look, as Baraq pursued Sisera, Yaʽěl came out to meet him, and said to him, “Come, and I show you the man whom you seek.” And when he went into her tent, there lay Sisera, dead with the peg in his temple. [23] So on that day <dn>Elohim</dn> humbled Jabin sovereign of Kenaʽan in the presence of the children of Israel. [24] And the hand of the children of Israel grew stronger and stronger against Jabin sovereign of Kenaʽan, until they had cut off Jabin sovereign of Kenaʽan.

readings.title: The Song of Victory
readings.subtitle: Deborah and Baraq Sing to YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Judges 5:1] Then Deborah and Baraq son of Abinoam sang on that day, saying, [2] “When leaders lead in Israel, when the people volunteer, bless <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! [3] “Hear, O sovereigns! Give ear, O rulers! I, to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, I sing! I sing praise to <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Israel. [4] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, when <dn>You</dn> went out from Sěʽir, when <dn>You</dn> stepped from the field of Edom, the earth trembled and the heavens dropped, the clouds also dropped water. [5] “The mountains flowed at the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, this Sinai at the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Israel. [6] “In the days of Shamgar, son of Anath, in the days of Yaʽěl, the highways were deserted, and the travelers walked in crooked ways. [7] “Leadership ceased, it ceased in Israel, until I, Deborah, arose, a mother in Israel arose. [8] “They chose new mighty ones, then there was fighting at the gates. Not a shield or spear was seen among forty thousand in Israel. [9] “My heart is with the rulers of Israel who offered themselves willingly with the people. Bless <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! [10] “You who ride on white donkeys, who sit on rich carpets, and who walk along the road, speak! [11] “By the voice of those who divide flocks at the watering places, there they recount the righteous acts of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the righteous acts of <dn>His</dn> leadership in Israel, then the people of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall go down to the gates. [12] “Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, sing a song! Arise, Baraq, and lead your captives away, O son of Abinoam! [13] “Then the survivor came down to the nobles; the people of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came down to me against the mighty. [14] “From Ephraim were those whose root is in Amalěq. After you, Binyamin, with your peoples. From Makir rulers came down, and from Zebulun those who bear the scribe’s staff. [15] “And the princes of Yissasḵar were with Deborah. And Yissasḵar, true to Baraq, rushed into the valley at his feet. Among the divisions of Reuben there were great resolves of heart. [16] “Why did you sit among the sheepfolds, to hear the pipings for the flocks? The divisions of Reuben have great searchings of heart. [17] “Gilʽaḏ abode beyond the Yarden. And Dan, why did he serve on ships? Asher sat at the seacoast, and abode by his creeks. [18] “Zebulun is a people who risked their lives to the point of death, Naphtali also, on the heights of the field. [19] “Sovereigns came and fought, then the sovereigns of Kenaʽan fought in Taʽanak, by the waters of Megiddo – they took no gain of silver. [20] “They fought from the heavens, the stars from their courses fought against Sisera. [21] “The torrent of Qishon swept them away, that ancient torrent, the torrent of Qishon. O my being, march on in strength! [22] “Then the horses’ hooves beat, from the galloping, the galloping of his mighty ones. [23] <dq>‘Curse Meroz,’</dq> said the <dn>Messenger of YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Curse its inhabitants bitterly, because they did not come to the help of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to the help of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> against the mighty.’</dq> [24] “Blessed above women is Yaʽěl, the wife of Ḥeber the Qěynite – blessed is she above women in the tent. [25] “He asked for water, she gave milk. She brought out curd in a magnificent bowl. [26] “She stretched her hand to the tent peg, and her right hand to the workmen’s hammer. And she hammered Sisera, she smashed his head, and she pierced and struck through his temple. [27] “Between her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay. Between her feet he bowed, he fell. Where he bowed, there he fell, destroyed. [28] “The mother of Sisera looked through the window, and cried out through the lattice, ‘Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why do the steps of his chariots delay?’ [29] “The wise ones of her ladies answered her, she also answered herself, [30] ‘Have they not found, are they not dividing the spoil? A girl, two girls for every man; a spoil of dyed garments for Sisera, a spoil of dyed garments, embroidery, two dyed garments for the necks of the spoil?’ [31] “Thus let all <dn>Your</dn> enemies perish, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! But let those who love <dn>Him</dn> be like the sun when it comes out in its might.” And the land had rest for forty years.

readings.title: The Oppression of Midian
readings.subtitle: Israel Cries Out Again
readings.text: [Judges 6:1] And the children of Israel did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave them into the hand of Midian for seven years. [2] And the hand of Midian prevailed against Israel. Because of the Midianites, the children of Israel made for themselves the hiding places which are in the mountains, and the caves and the strongholds. [3] And it came to be, when Israel had sown, that Midian would come up, and Amalěq, and the people of the East would come up against them. [4] And they encamped against them and destroyed the increase of the earth as far as Azzah, and left no sustenance for Israel, neither sheep nor ox nor donkey. [5] For they would come up with their livestock and their tents, coming in as numerous as locusts. Both they and their camels were without number. And they came into the land to destroy it. [6] And Israel became very poor because of the Midianites, and the children of Israel cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [7] And it came to be, when the children of Israel cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> because of the Midianites, [8] that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent a prophet to the children of Israel, who said to them, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Israel, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> brought you up from Mitsrayim, and brought you out of the house of bondage.</dq> [9] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> delivered you out of the hand of the Mitsrites and out of the hand of all who oppressed you, and drove them out before you and gave you their land.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> said to you, “<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, do not fear the mighty ones of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell.” But you have not obeyed <dn>My</dn> voice.’</dq> ”

readings.title: The Call of Gid'on
readings.subtitle: The Mighty Man of Valour
readings.text: [11] And the <dn>Messenger of YeHoVaH</dn> came and sat under the terebinth tree which was in Ophrah, which belonged to Joash the Abiʽezerite, while his son Gidʽon threshed wheat in the winepress, to hide it from the eyes of the Midianites. [12] And the <dn>Messenger of YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to him, and said to him, <dq>“<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with you, you mighty man of valour!”</dq> [13] And Gidʽon said to <dn>Him</dn>, “O my master, if <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with us, why then has all this come upon us? And where are all <dn>His</dn> miracles which our fathers told us about, saying, ‘Did not <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> bring us up from Mitsrayim?’ But now <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has forsaken us and given us into the hand of Midian.” [14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> turned to him and said, <dq>“Go in this strength of yours, and you shall save Israel from the hand of Midian. Have <dn>I</dn> not sent you?”</dq> [15] And he said to <dn>Him</dn>, “O my <dn>Master</dn>, with what do I save Israel? See, my clan is the weakest in Menashsheh, and I am the least in my father’s house.” [16] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“But <dn>I</dn> shall be with you, and you shall smite the Midianites as one man.”</dq> [17] And he said to <dn>Him</dn>, “Please, if I have found favour in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, then <dn>You</dn> shall show me a sign that it is <dn>You</dn> who speak with me. [18] “Please do not turn away from here until I come to <dn>You</dn>, and bring out my offering and set it before <dn>You</dn>.” And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall stay until you return.”</dq> [19] And Gidʽon went in and prepared a young goat, and unleavened bread from an ěphah of flour. The meat he put in a basket, and he put the broth in a pot. And he brought them out to <dn>Him</dn> under the terebinth tree and presented them. [20] And the <dn>Messenger of Elohim</dn> said to him, <dq>“Take the meat and the unleavened bread and lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth.”</dq> And he did so. [21] And the <dn>Messenger of YeHoVaH</dn> put out the end of the staff that was in <dn>His</dn> hand, and touched the meat and the unleavened bread. And fire rose out of the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened bread. And the <dn>Messenger of YeHoVaH</dn> went from his eyes. [22] And Gidʽon saw that <dn>He</dn> was the <dn>Messenger of YeHoVaH</dn>, and Gidʽon said, “Alas, O <dn>Master YeHoVaH</dn>! Because I have seen the <dn>Messenger of YeHoVaH</dn> face to face.” [23] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Peace be with you. Do not fear, you shall not die.”</dq> [24] And Gidʽon built an altar there to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and called it: <dn>YeHoVaH Shalom</dn>. To this day it is still in Ophrah of the Abiʽezerites.

readings.title: Tearing Down the Altar
readings.subtitle: Gid'on Contends with Ba'al
readings.text: [25] And it came to be on that night that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Take your father’s young bull, the second bull of seven years old, and you shall throw down the altar of Baʽal that your father has, and cut down the Ashěrah that is beside it,</dq> [26] <dq>and build an altar to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> on top of this stronghold in an orderly manner, and take the second bull and offer a burnt offering with the wood of the Ashěrah which you cut down.”</dq> [27] So Gidʽon took ten men from among his servants and did as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said to him. And it came to be, because he feared his father’s household and the men of the city too much to do it by day, that he did it by night. [28] And when the men of the city arose early in the morning, see, the altar of Baʽal was broken down, and the Ashěrah that was beside it was cut down, and the second bull was being offered on the altar which had been built. [29] And they said to each other, “Who has done this deed?” And when they inquired and asked, they said, “Gidʽon son of Joash has done this deed.” [30] Then the men of the city said to Joash, “Bring out your son, and let him die, because he has broken down the altar of Baʽal, and because he has cut down the Ashěrah that was beside it.” [31] And Joash said to all who stood against him, “Would you plead for Baʽal? Would you save him? Let the one who would plead for him be put to death by morning! If he is an elohim, let him plead for himself, because his altar has been broken down!” [32] So on that day he called him Yerubbaʽal, saying, “Let Baʽal plead against him, because he has broken down his altar.”

readings.title: The Sign of the Fleece
readings.subtitle: Testing the Word of Elohim
readings.text: [33] And all Midian and Amalěq and the people of the East gathered together, and they passed over and encamped in the Valley of Yizreʽěl. [34] And the <dn>Spirit of YeHoVaH</dn> came upon Gidʽon, and he blew the ram’s horn, and the Abiʽezerites were called to follow him. [35] And he sent messengers throughout all Menashsheh, who also were called to follow him. And he sent messengers to Asher, and to Zebulun, and to Naphtali, and they came up to meet them. [36] And Gidʽon said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “If <dn>You</dn> are saving Israel by my hand as <dn>You</dn> have said – [37] see, I am placing a fleece of wool on the threshing-floor. If there is dew on the fleece only, and it is dry on all the ground, then I shall know that <dn>You</dn> save Israel by my hand, as <dn>You</dn> have said.” [38] And it was so. And he rose early the next morning and squeezed the fleece together, and wrung the dew out of the fleece, a bowl full of water. [39] And Gidʽon said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Do not let <dn>Your</dn> displeasure burn against me, and let me speak but once more. Please let me test, I pray, just once more with the fleece. Let it now be dry on the fleece only, but on all the ground let there be dew.” [40] And <dn>Elohim</dn> did so that night. And it was dry on the fleece only, but there was dew on all the ground.
